propositions: Five measured test modules repeatedly construct equivalent virgin git and rebar stores from scratch for each test consumer despite invariant fixture topology, consuming 103.416 of 380.393 aggregate worker-seconds in fixture_setup spans.
Runtime profiling confirms each store build dominates setup latency (0.426s–1.445s real vs 0.031s–0.126s per isolated copy), with 12–23× speedup from per-test copies of session-scoped templates.

The clone_topology_template helper copies .opcert-key and .opcert-key.pub verbatim without reminting per-environment identity, causing clones with distinct .env-id to share one private signing key and violate the acceptance criterion that per-test copies cannot share signing keys.

Consensus from Django, Rails, and GitLab codebase practices (3/3 OSS projects actively using session templates with per-test copy/reset; no rejections found) and prior closed ticket peculiar-calmy-bubblefish (31% wall-time improvement, 270.7s→186.5s) establishes legitimacy of isolated fixture reuse where rollback/copy is faithful.

Proposed remediation requires that per-test fixture copies isolate all mutable state (refs, worktree paths, environment identity, signing keys, module caches), retain virgin templates, preserve from-scratch initialization/recovery tests, and validate isolation with sentinel tests that fail on shared refs, copied keys, or template mutation.
